To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a methodology for risk analysis in production processes that combines business process modeling and FCMs for risk identification and two fuzzy systems for risk evaluation.

the proposed methodology can be used to identify and evaluate risks in production processes and that it is based on the combination of BPMN and FCM to model and represent production processes and risks, and of two fuzzy systems to compute risk impact and risk priority index.

the integration of BPMN and FCMs in a single methodology allows a structured and formal description of a production process and its related risk, the integration of fuzzy systems in the methodology allows a better control of the ambiguity that often characterizes risk evaluation, the proposed methodology can be easily adopted by the risk analyst and it allows the risk analyst to better understand how risks might influence each other.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of an integrated approach based on BPMN and FCMs to represent the production process flow and the cause effect relations between risks and their possible causes, respectively, and on fuzzy systems to compute risk impact and priority.
the development of a methodology for risk analysis in production processes.
a methodology for risk analysis in production processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach allows the risk manager to identify, analyze and evaluate the risk in a production process.

our proposed approach is able to identify and evaluate the risks of a given production process, in an effective manner, by taking into account the ambiguity and the vagueness of subjective risk evaluation, as well as by providing a clear and formal description of the process itself.
the proposed methodology is an effective way of identifying risks and assessing their priority in a given production process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our methodology is a useful tool for identifying and evaluating risks in production processes and, as such, could be adopted by companies to improve their production processes.

the proposed methodology allows us to: (1) identify the risks related to a production process, (2) evaluate the risk priority index, (3) provide a better understanding of the cause effect relationships among risks and their causes, (4) associate each risk to the part/activity of production process in which it might be generated, and (5) provide better tolerance and management of ambiguity and vaguenesses that are often involved during the risk identification and evaluation phases.

we have proposed an integrated approach for risk identification and analysis in a context of a production process, where we have used two different graphic notations, BPMN and FCMs, for the description of the process itself and the risk/causes relationships, respectively, and we have used two fuzzy systems for the evaluation of risk impact and priority index.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed integrated methodology allows risk identification and evaluation to be performed in a systematic manner, thus making the whole process more effective.

the use of fuzzy systems allows us to deal with the ambiguity and vaguencess that are usually associated with risk evaluation, while the use of the two different graphical notations allows us to provide a better representation of the risk management context.
the combination of the two graphic notations and the two fuzzy systems allows us to better identify and manage risks in production processes.
